mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the prior month signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days regardless of regime conditions.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods where FEDFUNDS declines by at least 0.10 percentage points over the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.0% for two consecutive months, it signals restrictive monetary policy that increases corporate borrowing costs and reduces earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 45% of periods where FEDFUNDS remains above 4.0% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and rise in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) signals a weakening housing market combined with persistent inflation, triggering equity sell-offs and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint condition of HOUST declining and CPIAUCSL rising fails to produce negative 5-day returns in more than 55% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: In a low-unemployment regime (UNRATE < 4.0%), payroll growth exceeding 200,000 jobs (PAYEMS > 200000) signals robust labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where UNRATE < 4.0% and PAYEMS > 200000, S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate (UNRATE) over the prior month indicates deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer confidence and corporate hiring, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days regardless of regime conditions.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods where UNRATE increases by at least 0.10 percentage points over the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: When consumer spending (RSAFS) falls below 440,000 million dollars for two consecutive months, it signals a contraction in household consumption that reduces corporate revenue growth, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 45% of periods where RSAFS remains below 440000 for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals manufacturing contraction amid monetary tightening, depressing corporate earnings and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint condition of INDPRO declining and FEDFUNDS rising fails to produce negative 20-day returns in more than 55% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: In a high-inflation regime (CPIAUCSL > 3.0% YoY), a decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 0.5% signals aggressive monetary easing that initially boosts equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where CPIAUCSL > 3.0% and FEDFUNDS declines below 0.5%, S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of cases.
